items.title: 93% of paint splatters are valid Perl programs (2019)
items.author: zenincognito
items.summary: According to the sources, an empirical study conducted by Colin McMillen found that 93% of paint splatters parse as valid Perl programs when analyzed using optical character recognition (OCR) software. The study analyzed 100 images and found that 93 out of 100 images successfully parsed as valid Perl programs under at least one combination of Tesseract OCR engine and page segmentation mode. The study also presented seven examples of paint splatters which did not parse as valid Perl programs.

items.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers
items.author: herpderperator
items.summary: United Airlines announced on November 11 that it is banning personal AI agents from booking flights to protect customer data and comply with Federal Aviation Administration and Department of Transportation rules. The ban applies to its platform as well as travel agencies and aggregators. While AI agents can still show flight options and prices, they can't directly purchase tickets on United's website. The airline cited concerns about customer data, unintended purchases, and regulatory compliance as reasons for the ban. This move follows similar restrictions by other companies, including banks and Amazon, which have also limited AI agents' access to their platforms.

items.title: Gemini Decisions API
items.author: iamdelirium
items.summary: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, 2026, through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio. This API, powered by Gemini Decision 1, evaluates up to 1,000 independent questions across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs in one request. It is designed for bounded judgments such as tool selection, policy checks, model routing, context grading, and ranking. Developers can use Python, JavaScript, or REST, and the SDK quickstarts require `google-genai` 3.2 or later. The API supports prototyping with a no-cost AI Studio tier and is integrated with OpenRouter, LangChain, Vercel, LiteLLM, Pydantic AI, Pipecat, LiveKit, and OpenCode. Gemini in Google Cloud support is listed as coming soon.

items.title: Did Life Begin in an RNA World?
items.author: acossta
items.summary: New experiments support the "RNA world" hypothesis, suggesting that RNA, a simpler molecule than DNA, formed first and could have been a main player in the origin of life on Earth. According to the Space article, RNA's ability to carry genetic information and create other molecules supports this hypothesis. The Wikipedia article notes that although alternative paths to life have been proposed, the RNA world hypothesis is the most favored abiogenesis paradigm. The Memesita article dates Earth's transition into a cradle for life to 4.33 billion years ago, based on a study published in Nature Communications. However, the RNA world model does not account for every environmental factor, and the exact timeline and conditions remain uncertain.

items.title: My AI agents found an unmapped Maya site?
items.author: eyvindn
items.summary: According to the sources, the claim that AI agents discovered an unmapped Maya site in Mexico using NASA LiDAR data is not entirely accurate. While the AI agents identified potential structures, Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) confirmed that no archaeological site was registered at that location. Additionally, the site had already been discovered and published in a 2025 paper by Estrada-Belli, Canuto, Šprajc & Fernandez-Diaz. Therefore, the site was not truly unmapped or unknown.

items.title: How to make a CNC plasma cutter with high-frequency start
items.author: edward
items.summary: To make a CNC plasma cutter with high-frequency (HF) start, you need to use a cutter that relies on HF ignition, which is effective but generates electromagnetic interference (EMI). HF ignition involves a dedicated HF generator and proper shielding/grounding to mitigate stray EMI, which is important in environments with sensitive electronics. HF start cutters need direct electrical contact with the workpiece to start the cutting action, making them common in industrial CNC plasma tables where EMI is managed. To connect the torch trigger wires, PWM signal, positive power, and ground from the CNC controller, follow the wiring instructions provided in the sources: connect the torch trigger wires to the normally open contacts on the terminal block, the PWM signal to the white or yellow wire, the positive power to the red wire, and the ground to the black wire.

items.title: Faster Retrieval for Better, More Efficient RAG
items.author: zerop
items.summary: To achieve faster retrieval for better, more efficient RAG, the sources suggest leveraging smarter chunking techniques like recursive character text splitting and sliding window overlap to maintain context and reduce noise. They also highlight the use of hybrid retrieval approaches that combine different methods to improve accuracy and relevance. Additionally, utilizing platforms like Nexla with accelerated embedding and retrieval through NVIDIA AI, and scalable RAG workflows can significantly enhance the speed and efficiency of data retrieval and reranking processes. These methods collectively aim to provide more precise and contextually relevant outputs in RAG systems.

items.summary: Filament is an open-source Laravel admin panel framework built on Livewire and the TALL stack. It provides a form builder, table builder, notifications, and widgets to quickly create admin UIs without much front-end code. However, it is not a pre-built CMS; it does not offer a REST content API, multi-project dashboard, or turnkey install-and-manage-content experience. For development, SQLite is recommended due to its zero setup, no server needed, fast, and portable nature. For production, upgrade to PostgreSQL or MySQL is suggested. Filament is lightweight and stays within your Laravel application, unlike WordPress which is considered bloated.

items.title: Atuin Threads: All your agent sessions on every machine
items.author: linsomniac
items.summary: Atuin 18.24 introduces Threads, a feature that syncs AI coding agent sessions across machines, allowing users to resume or fork sessions in different agents. It supports sessions in Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Omp, and OpenCode, with end-to-end encrypted syncing that can use Atuin's hosted server, a self-hosted one, or local capture, all of which are opt-in. An MCP server, installed via 'atuin mcp install', enables agents to search and reference past sessions themselves. To start, install with the setup script and run 'atuin resume'. Threads is an extension of Atuin's original concept of making the history of your work useful, accessible, and private.

items.title: Apple has new Mac app coming to make running local AI models easy
items.author: linolevan
items.summary: Leaker Aaron Perris has discovered evidence of a new Mac app in the works at Apple called Harbor, which makes it easy to run local AI models across one or more Macs. The app turns your Mac into a private AI inference server, allowing open-weight models to run locally on Apple silicon with data never leaving your hardware and nothing reaching the cloud. Users can connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory, enabling large models and higher concurrency that a single computer can handle alone.

items.title: A2UI 1.0
items.author: zeroasterisk
items.summary: A2UI 1.0 is a release candidate as per the official website and GitHub repository. It adds client-to-server RPC (`actionResponse`), action IDs, and renames theme to surfaceProperties. The official MIME type has been standardized to `application/a2ui+json` to conform to IANA media type guidelines. The evolution guide details the changes from version 0.9, including setting the `version` field in all streamed JSON envelopes to `"1.0"`, changing the MIME type of A2UI payloads in transport layers from `application/json+a2ui` to `application/a2ui+json`, and removing the `theme` field from `createSurface` messages.

items.title: Tools for exploring the souls of large language models
items.author: r00tanon
items.summary: The sources mention several tools for exploring the souls of large language models (LLMs), including TinyGPT Visualizer, TransformerViz, TransformerLens, ecco, verified-circuits, Circuit Lantern, PTS, and Neurolume. These tools are part of the growing field of mechanistic interpretability, which aims to decode how LLMs think and act. The TinyGPT Visualizer is specifically noted for its role in decoding the inner workings of LLMs, while other tools like verified-circuits offer independently-checkable mechanistic interpretability. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to the question but highlight these tools as part of the ongoing research in this area.

items.title: I Accidentally Became a Millionaire
items.author: OuterVale
items.summary: According to the sources, becoming a millionaire can happen through various means, often unexpectedly. One individual became a millionaire at 30 after selling their business and investing the proceeds conservatively in the stock market. This person emphasized long-term business investment and multiple income sources. Another story involves Timothy Dexter, known as one of History's Biggest Idiots, who became a millionaire despite poor business decisions due to his unique circumstances. The Hacker News discussion suggests that becoming wealthy can lead to a loss of drive, with suggestions ranging from buying an airplane to investing in Vanguard funds. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to how one becomes a millionaire but highlight different paths and experiences.
